habitat.naturalHabitat: Soil, sewage, and the GI tract of humans and animals
habitat.hostAssociation: Normal gut flora; opportunistic pathogen in wounds and contaminated food
habitat.environmentalOccurrence: Widespread in soil and decaying matter

microscopy.appearance: Large Gram-positive rods, spores rarely seen in clinical specimens

culture.growthCharacteristics: Obligate anaerobe but aerotolerant; extremely rapid growth (generation time ~10 min)
culture.hemolysis: Double zone of hemolysis (inner complete beta from theta toxin, outer incomplete from alpha toxin)

identificationClues: Double zone of hemolysis on blood agar
Rapid growth — generation time of about 10 minutes
Associated with gas gangrene and food poisoning

virulenceFactors: Alpha toxin (lecithinase/phospholipase C — key virulence factor in gas gangrene)
clinicalImportance.transmission: Wound contamination with soil/spores; foodborne via improperly held cooked meats and gravies
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: Common cause of traumatic and surgical wound gas gangrene; a leading cause of bacterial food poisoning worldwide
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: Nagler reaction (lecithinase activity inhibited by specific antitoxin) confirms alpha toxin production

examFacts.importantTest: Nagler reaction; double zone hemolysis on blood agar
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: Extremely rapid generation time and double-zone hemolysis distinguish it from other clostridia
